patterns.kid_explanation: OptiFine and Sodium are fighting! 🥊 They both try to make Minecraft run faster and look prettier, but they do it in different ways that don't work together. You can only use one at a time!
patterns.fix: Remove OptiFine OR remove Sodium (not both!). Sodium is usually faster, so keep Sodium and remove OptiFine. Just delete the OptiFine .jar file from your mods folder.

patterns.kid_explanation: Minecraft ran out of memory! 🎮 It's like trying to fit too many toys in a small box - there just isn't enough space. This usually happens when you have lots of mods loaded or your render distance is really high.
patterns.fix: Give Minecraft more RAM in your launcher settings. Try 4-6 GB if you have mods. Also try lowering your render distance to 12 or less.

patterns.kid_explanation: A mod tried to change Minecraft's code, but something went wrong! 🔧 This usually means two mods are trying to change the same thing in different ways.
patterns.fix: Try updating your mods to the latest versions. If that doesn't work, try removing mods one at a time to find which ones don't work together.

patterns.kid_explanation: Something in Minecraft tried to use something that doesn't exist! 🤔 It's like reaching for a toy that isn't there. This is usually a bug in a mod.
patterns.fix: Try updating your mods to the latest versions. If the crash keeps happening, report it to the mod author on CurseForge or GitHub with your crash log.

patterns.kid_explanation: A mod is looking for another mod (or library) that you don't have installed! 📦 It's like trying to play a game without all the pieces.
patterns.fix: Check which mods are required by reading the mod description on CurseForge. Install any required mods or libraries (like Fabric API, Cloth Config, or Architectury).

patterns.kid_explanation: You're trying to use a Fabric mod with Forge (or vice versa)! ⚠️ Fabric and Forge are two different ways to load mods - they don't mix!
patterns.fix: Make sure all your mods are for the same mod loader (all Fabric OR all Forge). Check the mod page to see which loader it needs.

patterns.kid_explanation: Something went wrong with a creature or item in your world! 🐑 Usually this is caused by a corrupted entity (like a mob or dropped item).
patterns.fix: Try using a tool like MCEdit to remove the broken entity. The crash log should show coordinates - go there and look for weird mobs or items.

patterns.regex: Exception ticking block entity|Block entity being ticked
patterns.kid_explanation: A block in your world is causing problems! 🧱 This could be a machine from a mod, a chest, or any special block.
patterns.fix: The crash log shows coordinates of the broken block. Go there and break/remove the block causing issues. If you can't get in-game, use MCEdit to remove it.

patterns.kid_explanation: Two parts of Minecraft tried to change the same thing at the exact same time! ⚡ It's like two people trying to write on the same paper at once.
patterns.fix: This is usually a mod bug. Try updating your mods. If it keeps happening, report it to the mod author with your crash log.

patterns.kid_explanation: Minecraft couldn't read or write a file! 💾 Maybe your disk is full, a file is corrupted, or you don't have permission to access it.
patterns.fix: Check if your disk is full. Make sure Minecraft has permission to read/write files. Try running Minecraft as administrator (Windows) or check file permissions (Mac/Linux).

patterns.kid_explanation: Your graphics card is having trouble! 🎨 This could be outdated drivers, incompatible shaders, or graphics settings that are too high.
patterns.fix: Update your graphics drivers. If using shaders, try disabling them or using simpler shader packs. Lower your graphics settings (especially particles and render distance).

patterns.kid_explanation: Minecraft tried to read a configuration file, but it's formatted wrong! 📝 Someone (or a mod) made a typo in a .json file.
patterns.fix: Check the crash log for which file is broken. Use a JSON validator online to fix the syntax. If it's from a mod, try reinstalling that mod or resetting its config.

patterns.kid_explanation: Two mods are trying to use the same crafting recipe! 🔨 Minecraft doesn't know which one to use.
patterns.fix: Usually this doesn't crash the game, just a warning. If it does crash, try removing one of the conflicting mods or use a mod like KubeJS to fix the recipe conflict.

patterns.kid_explanation: Minecraft is looking for something that used to be there but is gone now! 🔍 This happens when you remove a mod from a world that was using it.
patterns.fix: If you removed a mod, you might need to add it back temporarily. Or use a tool to clean missing registry entries from your world save.

patterns.kid_explanation: A mod is the wrong version! 🔢 Maybe it's for Minecraft 1.19 but you're running 1.20, or it needs a newer version of another mod.
patterns.fix: Check that all your mods match your Minecraft version. Update or downgrade mods as needed. Make sure dependencies (like Fabric API) are the right version too.
